en: to be emotionally moved; to be touched

examples.en: I was really moved after watching the movie.

examples.ko: 친구가 쓴 편지를 읽고 감동한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I was once touched after reading a letter my friend wrote.
I was moved by the song and cried.
I'm easily moved even by small kindnesses.

examples.ko: 그 이야기를 읽으면 누구나 감동할 거예요.
examples.en: Anyone who reads that story will be moved.

examples.ko: 이런 선물에도 감동하지 않는 사람이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who isn't touched by a gift like this?

explain: 사람이 주어이면 '감동하다'나 '감동받다'를 쓰고, 영화나 이야기가 주어이면 '감동적이다'를 써요. '영화가 감동적이에요', '저는 감동했어요'처럼 짝을 맞춰 보세요. '감동을 받았어요'도 아주 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 그 노래를 듣고 감동을 받았어요.
phrases.en: I was moved when I heard that song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감동하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 아주 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 감동하다 and very common in speech.

phrases.en: I was really touched by my friend's gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 마음이 움직인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for being emotionally moved.

phrases.en: This movie is really moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 이야기가 주어일 때 쓰는 형용사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective form used when a movie or story is the subject.

explain_en: When a person is the subject, use '감동하다' or '감동받다'; when a movie or story is the subject, use '감동적이다'. Compare '영화가 감동적이에요' and '저는 감동했어요'. '감동을 받았어요' is also very common.

examples.en: In summer, cold soup brings back your appetite.
I floated ice in the cold soup and ate it.
I put julienned cucumber into the cold soup.
The cold soup was so refreshing that I finished my rice quickly.
Please give me one more bowl of cold soup.
My mother made me cold soup.

explain: 차갑게 먹는 국이라서 따뜻한 국과 달라요. 오이냉국, 미역냉국처럼 앞에 재료 이름을 붙여서 많이 말해요. 여름 식탁에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: On hot days, I want to eat cold cucumber soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오이로 만든 대표적인 여름 냉국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical summer cold soup made with cucumber.

phrases.en: I made cold seaweed soup for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미역으로 만든 냉국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cold soup made with seaweed.

phrases.en: In summer, I eat cold soup with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 먹는다고 할 때 '먹다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 먹다 for eating soup.

explain_en: It is a soup eaten cold, unlike a hot soup. People often put the main ingredient before it, as in 오이냉국 (cucumber) and 미역냉국 (seaweed). You see it often on summer tables.

examples.en: The size of the pagoda is enormous.
It was the holiday season, so the airport was incredibly crowded.
They say the amount of rain yesterday was enormous.
That singer's popularity is truly tremendous.

examples.ko: 엄청난 소식을 들었는데, 우리 팀이 우승했대요!
examples.en: I heard huge news: our team won the championship!

explain: 크기나 양이 상상보다 클 때 써요. 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 써서 '엄청난 인기', '엄청난 실수' 모두 가능해요. 말할 때는 부사 '엄청'만 써서 '엄청 맛있어요'라고도 해요.

dict_examples.en: The scale of the business is enormous.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 일이 너무 엄청나서 엄두가 나지 않았다.
dict_examples.en: The task was so huge that I couldn't bring myself to try.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Used when size or amount is bigger than you imagined. It works for good and bad: '엄청난 인기' and '엄청난 실수' both work. In speech people also use just '엄청' as an adverb: '엄청 맛있어요'.

en: to be rather embarrassed; to be rather bewildered; to be rather disconcerted

examples.en: My name was suddenly called, and I was flustered.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 말을 걸어서 좀 당황스러워요.
examples.en: A stranger talked to me, and I'm a bit flustered.

examples.ko: 약속 장소를 잘못 알았다니 당황스러운 일이에요.
examples.en: It's a bewildering thing to have the wrong meeting place.
Much to my dismay, I left my wallet at home.

examples.ko: 면접에서 예상 못 한 질문을 받으면 당황스럽지요.
examples.en: It's disconcerting to get a question you didn't expect in an interview.

examples.ko: 친구가 갑자기 화를 내서 당황스럽다고 느꼈어요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly got angry and I felt thrown off.

explain: '당황하다'는 놀라서 어쩔 줄 모르는 사람의 모습이고, '당황스럽다'는 상황이 그런 마음이 들게 한다는 느낌이에요. '황당하다'는 어이가 없을 때, '당황스럽다'는 어떻게 해야 할지 모를 때 써요.

phrases.example: 비행기를 놓친 건 정말 당황스러운 상황이었어요.
phrases.en: Missing the plane was a really bewildering situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '당황스럽다'를 '-ㄴ' 꼴로 바꿔 '상황', '일'을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective changes to its -ㄴ form to describe 상황 or 일.

phrases.en: My friend who was asked the question looked flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone looks that way from the outside.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and everyone was flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 놀라서 어쩔 줄 모르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who is so startled they do not know what to do.

explain_en: '당황하다' describes a person who is startled and at a loss, while '당황스럽다' says the situation makes you feel that way. '황당하다' is for absurd things that leave you speechless; '당황스럽다' is for not knowing what to do.

examples.en: My father works as a professor at a university in the provinces.
To become a university professor, you need a doctorate.
When I was young, I dreamed of becoming a professor.
He is a famous professor, so he gives many lectures.
I sent my question to the professor by email.
The professor's office is on the fourth floor.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '대학교수'를 쓰고, 직접 부를 때는 '교수님'이라고 해요. 이름 뒤에도 '김 교수님'처럼 '교수님'을 붙여요. '선생님'보다 '교수님'이 대학에서는 더 정확한 호칭이에요.

phrases.en: Professor, I have a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교수를 직접 부를 때는 '교수님'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when addressing a university professor directly.

phrases.en: Professor Kim's class is interesting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성 뒤에 '교수님'을 붙여 존경을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 교수님 after the surname shows respect.

phrases.en: I want to become a university professor someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 목표로 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for talking about a career goal.

explain_en: Use '대학교수' to name the job, but when addressing the person, say '교수님'. After a surname you attach '교수님' too, as in '김 교수님'. At a university, '교수님' is the more accurate title than '선생님'.

examples.ko: 비가 그친 뒤 길에 물웅덩이가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, many puddles formed on the road.
The child jumped over a small puddle.

examples.ko: 운전할 때 물웅덩이 옆을 지나면 물이 튀어요.
examples.en: When driving, water splashes if you pass next to a puddle.
The kids splashed around in the puddle.
The sky was reflected in the puddle, and it looked pretty.
Please be careful and go around the puddles.

explain: 그냥 '웅덩이'라고 해도 되지만, 비 온 뒤 고인 물을 분명히 말할 때 '물웅덩이'를 써요. '밟다, 튀다, 피하다, 뛰어넘다'와 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: I stepped in a puddle by mistake and my socks got wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웅덩이에 발을 넣게 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when your foot lands in a puddle.

phrases.example: 신발이 젖을까 봐 물웅덩이를 피해서 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I walked around the puddles so my shoes wouldn't get wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 온 뒤 길을 걸을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when walking after rain.

phrases.example: 비가 오면 이 길에는 물웅덩이가 생겨요.
phrases.en: When it rains, puddles form on this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 와서 물이 고였다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say water collected after rain.

explain_en: You can just say '웅덩이', but '물웅덩이' makes clear it is standing water, like after rain. It often appears with verbs like 밟다, 튀다, 피하다 and 뛰어넘다.

examples.ko: 옥상에 있는 물탱크를 이번 주에 청소해요.
examples.en: They are cleaning the water tank on the roof this week.

examples.ko: 물탱크에 물이 얼마나 남았는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check how much water is left in the tank.

examples.ko: 캠핑카 뒤쪽에 작은 물탱크가 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A small water tank is attached at the back of the camper.

examples.ko: 이 물탱크는 오래돼서 곧 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: This water tank is old, so we need to replace it soon.

examples.ko: 비가 안 와서 물탱크의 물이 거의 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: It hasn't rained, so the tank is almost out of water.

examples.ko: 물탱크 청소하는 날에는 물이 잠깐 끊겨요.
examples.en: On the day the tank is cleaned, the water is cut off for a while.

explain: 건물 옥상이나 지하, 캠핑카 등에 물을 모아 두는 통을 말해요. 건물 설비로는 '저수조'라는 말도 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 '물탱크'가 편하게 들려요.

phrases.en: We clean the water tank next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물에서 정기적으로 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for regular maintenance in a building.

phrases.en: It rained, so the water tank is full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탱크에 물이 넘칠 만큼 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the tank holds as much water as it can.

phrases.en: I filled the camper's water tank with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 넣어서 채우는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of filling it with water.

explain_en: It is a container that stores water on a building's roof or basement, or in a camper. Buildings also use the term '저수조', but '물탱크' sounds more natural in everyday talk.

examples.en: There are many strange fish in the deep sea.
I learned to dive to see under the sea in person.

examples.ko: 바닷속은 소리가 거의 안 들려서 아주 조용해요.
examples.en: There is almost no sound under the sea, so it is very quiet.

examples.ko: 친구가 찍어 준 바닷속 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The underwater photos my friend took are really pretty.
I saw a huge turtle under the sea off Jeju Island.
The deeper you go, the darker it gets under the sea.

explain: '바다 속'처럼 띄지 않고 '바닷속'으로 붙여 써요. 비슷한 '물속'은 수영장이나 강에도 쓰지만 바닷속은 바다에만 써요. '땅속', '산속'도 같은 방식으로 만든 말이에요.

phrases.en: The deep sea is very dark and quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '깊은'과 함께 써서 바다 아래 깊은 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with the adjective 깊은 to mean the deep part under the sea.

phrases.en: I met a big turtle under the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 바다 아래에서 일어나는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to talk about things that happen under the sea.

phrases.en: The world under the sea is really amazing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷속 풍경이나 생물 이야기를 할 때 '바닷속 + 명사'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 바닷속 + noun when talking about scenery or life under the sea.

explain_en: It is written as one word, '바닷속', not '바다 속'. The similar '물속' (in the water) also works for pools and rivers, but 바닷속 is only for the sea. '땅속' (underground) and '산속' (deep in the mountains) are made the same way.

examples.en: Lights came on one by one on the night street outside the window.
Unlike in the daytime, the night streets are quiet and lonely.
I walked the night streets with a friend and we talked.
This neighborhood's streets are well lit at night, so it's safe.

examples.ko: 비 오는 밤거리 풍경이 영화 같았어요.
examples.en: The scene of the street at night in the rain was like a movie.
Shall we head out to the night streets after dinner?

explain: '야경'은 밤에 보이는 경치 전체이고, '밤거리'는 거리 자체를 가리켜요. '밤거리를 걷다', '밤거리를 헤매다'처럼 걷거나 돌아다니는 동작과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: After dinner, I walked along the night streets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 거리를 걷는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a slow walk down the street.

phrases.en: I wandered around the night streets during my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적 없이 여기저기 다닌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests roaming around without a set goal.

phrases.en: Only footsteps could be heard on the quiet night street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 적은 밤의 거리를 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a night street with few people.

explain_en: '야경' is the whole night view, while '밤거리' points to the street itself. It pairs well with walking or wandering verbs, as in '밤거리를 걷다' and '밤거리를 헤매다'.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 하는 전시회는 정말 볼만해요.
examples.en: The exhibition this weekend is really worth seeing.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 평이 좋아서 볼만할 것 같아요.
examples.en: That movie has good reviews, so it seems worth watching.
Seoul has so many places worth seeing.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 드라마 중에 볼만한 게 있어요?
examples.en: Is there anything worth watching among the new dramas?

examples.ko: 벚꽃이 피면 이 길이 정말 볼만하네요.
examples.en: When the cherry blossoms bloom, this road is really a sight to see.
Yesterday's soccer match was really worth watching.

explain: 영화, 전시, 경치, 경기처럼 보는 것에 가치가 있을 때 써요. '볼 만하다'로 띄어 써도 돼요. 비슷한 명사로 '볼거리'(볼 만한 것)가 있어요.

phrases.en: Please recommend a movie worth watching this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙일 때는 '볼만한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 볼만한 before a noun.

phrases.en: This city has a lot of things to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼만한 것'을 한 단어로 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun meaning 'things worth seeing'.

phrases.en: That exhibition was not really worth seeing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기에 가치가 크지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not worth seeing.

explain_en: It is used for things you watch or look at, such as movies, exhibitions, scenery and games, when they are worth it. You can also write it with a space, '볼 만하다'. A related noun is '볼거리' (something worth seeing).

examples.en: A bulldozer is pushing the ground flat at the construction site.

examples.ko: 불도저 소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I could not sleep because of the bulldozer noise.
The child moved sand with a toy bulldozer.
I saw a big bulldozer up close for the first time.

examples.ko: 산 앞에 불도저도 있고 크레인도 서 있었어요.
examples.en: In front of the mountain there was a bulldozer and a crane too.

examples.ko: 이 불도저에는 앞에 큰 삽이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: This bulldozer has a big blade on the front.

explain: 앞에 넓은 판이 달려 흙을 밀어내는 기계예요. 땅을 파는 기계는 '포클레인'이라고 부르는 경우가 많고, 정식 이름은 '굴착기'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 한번 마음먹으면 막힘없이 밀고 나가는 모습을 말해요.

phrases.en: push ahead regardless of opposition
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 다른 의견을 듣지 않고 힘차게 일을 진행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person drives a job forward forcefully without listening to other opinions.

explain_en: It has a wide blade on the front that pushes soil. The machine that digs the ground is often called '포클레인', and its formal name is '굴착기'. Used about a person, it describes someone who pushes ahead without stopping once they decide.

examples.en: The presenter explained with big hand gestures.
The hand movements were funny, so everyone laughed.
Sign language is a language spoken with hand movements.
The hand movements are too fast for me to follow.

examples.ko: 손동작 하나만 봐도 요리 실력이 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can feel someone's cooking skill from a single hand movement.

examples.ko: 노래에 맞춰 손동작도 같이 해 보세요.
examples.en: Try doing the hand movements along with the song.

explain: 손을 움직이는 모양이나 방법을 말해요. 누구를 부르거나 가리키는 손의 움직임은 '손짓'이라고 해요. 몸 전체를 쓰는 건 '몸짓'이라고 하고, 노래나 춤에 맞춘 손의 움직임은 '손동작'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Try to copy the teacher's hand movements.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래나 체조에서 동작을 흉내 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when copying movements in a song or exercise.

phrases.example: 요리사의 손동작이 빨라서 눈으로 따라가기 어려워요.
phrases.en: The chef's hands move so fast that it's hard to follow with my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손을 움직이는 속도나 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the speed or manner of hand movement.

phrases.en: We couldn't understand each other, so I explained with hand gestures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말 대신 손으로 뜻을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when conveying meaning with your hands instead of words.

explain_en: It refers to the shape or way the hands move. A hand movement for beckoning or pointing is called '손짓'. Using the whole body is '몸짓', and hand movements that go with a song or dance are naturally '손동작'.

examples.en: I changed the bed sheet.
The sheet was dirty, so I put it in the washing machine.
I spread a sheet over the sofa.

examples.ko: 차 시트가 너무 뜨거워서 앉기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The car seat is so hot that it's hard to sit.
I installed a child safety seat.
I peeled one off the sticker sheet and stuck it on.

explain: 시트는 침대에 깔거나 덮는 얇은 천을 말해요. 자동차나 비행기의 앉는 자리인 '좌석'도 시트라고 불러요. 침대 시트는 '이불'과 달리 위에 덮는 두꺼운 것이 아니에요.

phrases.en: I put a clean sheet on the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 침대 위에 시트를 펴서 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for spreading a sheet over a bed.

phrases.en: I wash the bed sheets every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더러워진 시트를 빨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when washing dirty sheets.

phrases.en: The new car seat is very comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이 아니라 자동차의 앉는 자리를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means the car seat, not a cloth sheet.

explain_en: 시트 is the thin cloth spread over or under a bed. It is also used for the seat of a car or plane, which is also called '좌석'. A bed sheet is not the same as an '이불', which is the thicker cover.

examples.en: At the zoo, the crocodile opened its mouth wide.
A crocodile stays hidden in the water for a long time.
I saw a crocodile up close for the first time.
It is dangerous to go near a crocodile.
A crocodile's teeth are very sharp.
Crocodiles also lay eggs and raise their young.

explain: 영어의 crocodile과 alligator를 한국어에서는 보통 둘 다 '악어'라고 불러요. '악어가죽 가방'처럼 가죽 이름으로도 써요.

phrases.en: That apology is nothing but crocodile tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속으로는 슬프지 않으면서 겉으로만 우는 척할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone only pretends to cry or feel sorry without really meaning it.

explain_en: Korean usually calls both the English 'crocodile' and 'alligator' '악어'. It also names the leather, as in '악어가죽 가방'.

examples.ko: 텔레비전 안테나가 부러져서 화면이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The TV antenna is broken, so there is no picture.
My father put an antenna on the roof.
A bird is sitting on the antenna.

examples.ko: 라디오 안테나는 길게 뽑아야 잘 잡혀요.
examples.en: You have to pull the radio antenna out long to get a good signal.
When I changed the direction of the antenna, I could hear the sound.
A robot shaped like an antenna is cute.

explain: 텔레비전이나 라디오 같은 기계에 달아 신호를 받는 장치예요. 휴대폰이 신호를 못 잡을 때는 '신호가 안 잡혀요', '안 터져요'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 새로운 소식이 없는지 안테나를 세우고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm keeping my antenna up for any new news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보나 소문에 민감하게 귀를 기울일 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative expression for staying alert to news or rumors.

explain_en: It is a device attached to machines such as TVs and radios to receive signals. When a phone cannot get reception, people say '신호가 안 잡혀요' or '안 터져요'.

examples.ko: 나뭇잎 위에 애벌레가 천천히 기어가고 있어요.
examples.en: A caterpillar is crawling slowly across the leaf.
A caterpillar goes through a chrysalis and becomes a butterfly.
I was startled to find a caterpillar in the cabbage field.
The child gave leaves to the caterpillar as food.
I get goosebumps just from seeing a caterpillar.

examples.ko: 초록색 애벌레 한 마리가 창문에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A green caterpillar is stuck to the window.

explain: 곤충은 '마리'로 세요. '애벌레 한 마리', '애벌레 두 마리'처럼 말해요. 나비의 애벌레처럼 어떤 곤충인지 말하고 싶을 때는 '나비 애벌레'라고 앞에 이름을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 풀잎 위에 애벌레 한 마리가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is one caterpillar on a blade of grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충은 '마리'로 세요. 숫자는 '한 마리', '두 마리'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Insects are counted with '마리': '한 마리', '두 마리'.

phrases.en: A butterfly caterpillar is eating a leaf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곤충의 애벌레인지 앞에 이름을 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the insect's name in front to say what kind of larva it is.

phrases.en: The caterpillar grows and becomes a pupa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기가 커지는 일은 '자라다'를 써요. 곤충이 변하는 과정을 말할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: '자라다' means growing bigger; good for describing an insect's changes.

explain_en: Insects are counted with '마리', as in '애벌레 한 마리'. To say which insect it belongs to, put the name before it, like '나비 애벌레'.

examples.en: My older sister is a stage actor.
To become a stage actor you need to practice your voice.
I met that stage actor and got an autograph.
Stage actors practice the same lines every day.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 연극배우로 살고 싶었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little I wanted to live as a stage actor.

examples.ko: 유명한 연극배우의 공연을 보러 극장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the theater to see a famous stage actor's performance.

explain: '배우'는 영화, 무대 등에서 연기하는 사람 모두를 가리키고, '연극배우'는 그중 무대에서 연기하는 사람이에요. '영화배우', '뮤지컬배우'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 어디서 연기하는지 구분해요.

phrases.en: I want to become a stage actor someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 장래 희망을 말할 때 '되다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 되다 (to become) when talking about dreams or future goals.

phrases.example: 삼촌은 십 년 동안 연극배우로 일했어요.
phrases.en: My uncle worked as a stage actor for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'를 붙여 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)로 to say what someone does for a living.
phrases.en_equiv: to work as a stage actor

phrases.en: That film actor started out as a stage actor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출신'을 붙이면 예전에 연극배우였다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 출신 means the person used to be a stage actor.

explain_en: 배우 covers anyone who acts in film, on stage and so on, and 연극배우 is the one who acts on stage. Adding a word in front, as in 영화배우 or 뮤지컬배우, tells you where the person performs.

examples.en: A gravel path is uncomfortable to walk on, so I wore sneakers.
Riding a bike on a gravel path shakes you a lot.
The country gravel path gets slippery when it rains.

examples.ko: 자갈길 끝에 작은 집이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small house at the end of the gravel path.
It's hard to go along a gravel path in high heels.
The car rattled as it passed over the gravel path.

explain: 길 앞에 바탕이 되는 말을 붙여 '흙길', '눈길', '빗길', '산길'처럼 길의 종류를 말해요. 자갈길도 그중 하나예요. '자갈길을 걷다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: Walking on a gravel path hurts my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '을/를'과 함께 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation with '을/를'.

phrases.en: The gravel path is bumpy, so you have to be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the state of the road.

phrases.en: When it rains, the dirt road gets slippery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자갈길'처럼 길의 바탕을 앞에 붙인 다른 길 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another road name built the same way, with the surface material in front.

explain_en: Korean puts the surface or setting before 길 to name a type of road, such as '흙길', '눈길', '빗길' and '산길'. 자갈길 is one of these. It goes with '을/를', as in '자갈길을 걷다'.

en: to be comic; to be funny

examples.en: The movie I saw yesterday is really comical.
That actor's performance was so comical.
A comical character is getting popular.
The way the kids danced comically was cute.

examples.ko: 코믹할 것 같아서 이 드라마를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose this drama because it seemed funny.
His voice is so comical that I keep laughing.

explain: '재미있다'는 모든 재미에 쓰지만, '코믹하다'는 웃기는 만화·영화·연기에 써요. 사람에게는 '웃기다'가 더 자연스러워요. 영어 comic에서 온 외래어예요.

phrases.en: When I watch a comic movie, I feel better.
phrases.nuance_ko: '코믹하다'를 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형으로, 웃기는 영화·만화·연기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '코믹하다', used before nouns like movie, comic, or acting.

phrases.en: The actor's face was so comic that I laughed a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이라 '웃었다' 같은 결과와 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form that gives a reason, often followed by a result like 'I laughed'.

phrases.en: This comic is not very funny.
phrases.nuance_ko: '코믹하다'의 부정 표현으로, 기대보다 웃기지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something is less funny than expected.

explain_en: '재미있다' covers every kind of fun, but 'komikhada' is for funny comics, films, and acting. For a person, '웃기다' sounds more natural. It is a loanword from English 'comic'.

en: to get excited; to get worked up; to become agitated

examples.en: The children got excited when they saw the presents.

examples.ko: 경기가 끝나자 관중이 흥분해서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: When the game ended, the crowd got worked up and shouted.
Don't get too worked up, let's talk calmly.
I was excited even before the concert started.
When I get worked up, my voice tends to get louder.
It's not something to get that worked up about, so please calm down.

explain: 기뻐서 들뜰 때도, 화가 나서 격해질 때도 써서 문장에서 느낌이 갈려요. 기쁜 쪽은 '신나다', '설레다', 화난 쪽은 '화내다'를 쓰면 더 분명해요. '흥분하지 마세요'는 화를 가라앉히라는 말로 들릴 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: Please do not get too worked up. Let's talk slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 났거나 격해진 사람에게 가라앉으라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said to someone who is angry or agitated, asking them to calm down.

phrases.en: Take a deep breath and calm down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들뜬 마음이나 화를 진정시킨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to settle down an excited or angry mind.

phrases.en: I am so excited because I am going on a trip tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기뻐서 들뜬 마음만 말할 때는 '신나다'가 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When you only mean being happily excited, 신나다 is clearer.

explain_en: It covers both being thrilled and being enraged, so the feeling depends on the sentence. For the happy side, '신나다' and '설레다' are clearer, and for anger, '화내다'. '흥분하지 마세요' often sounds like telling someone to calm down.

dis.h: get worked up, even angry; active

p.n: 흥분되다 describes the feeling; 흥분하다 describes getting worked up.
